11 An object is held in equilibrium by three forces. The forces all act in the same plane. The diagram
shows two of the forces that act on the object.
43 N
NOT TO
SCALE
125
17 N
The third force is missing from the diagram.
What is the third force?

hints: Notice the two given forces are $43\text{ N}$ vertically up and $17\text{ N}$ at $125^{\circ}$ to it, so resolve both into perpendicular components.
For equilibrium the vector sum must be zero, so the unknown third force must be equal and opposite to the resultant of the $43\text{ N}$ and $17\text{ N}$ forces.
Combine the components to find a resultant of about $36\text{ N}$ north-west, about $23^{\circ}$ west of north, then reverse its direction to get the equilibrant.
walkthrough: Take $+y$ as up and $+x$ as east. The $43\text{ N}$ force is $(0, 43)\text{ N}$.
The $17\text{ N}$ force is $125^{\circ}$ from $+y$ toward the south-west. Its components are $F_x = -17\sin 125^{\circ}$ and $F_y = 17\cos 125^{\circ}$.

With $\sin 125^{\circ} \approx 0.819$ and $\cos 125^{\circ} \approx -0.574$, $F_x \approx -13.9\text{ N}$ and $F_y \approx -9.8\text{ N}$. So the sum of the two forces is $F_x \approx -13.9\text{ N}$ and $F_y \approx 43 - 9.8 = 33.2\text{ N}$.
Resultant magnitude is $\sqrt{13.9^2 + 33.2^2} \approx 36\text{ N}$ directed north-west. Its angle west of north satisfies $\tan\theta = 13.9/33.2$, giving $\theta \approx 23^{\circ}$.

For equilibrium the third force must cancel this resultant, so it must be $36\text{ N}$ south-east, $23^{\circ}$ east of south. An angle of $157^{\circ}$ from north leaves $180^{\circ}-157^{\circ}=23^{\circ}$ to the south direction. This is option B.

A.explanation: This is $36\text{ N}$ acting to the north-west, which is the resultant of the $43\text{ N}$ and $17\text{ N}$ forces, not the equilibrant needed to give zero net force.

B.explanation: This is $36\text{ N}$ acting to the south-east, equal and opposite to the resultant of the $43\text{ N}$ and $17\text{ N}$ forces, so the three forces sum to zero.

C.explanation: This $55\text{ N}$ force to the north-east has too large a magnitude and the wrong direction to cancel the $43\text{ N}$ upward and $17\text{ N}$ south-west components.

D.explanation: This $55\text{ N}$ force to the south-west has too large a magnitude and does not balance the upward $33\text{ N}$ net vertical component.
